Infer the ADaM Dataset Class

Source: R/admiral_df.R
infer_dataset_class.Rd

Attempts to classify a data frame as one of the common ADaM dataset classes from its variables and records. It ignores any class declared with admiral_df(): get_dataset_class() returns the declared class if there is one, and only falls back to this function otherwise.

Note that this is the class of the dataset (ADSL, BDS, ...), not its record structure: the latter is the set of key variables which uniquely identify its records. Unlike the class, the keys are never inferred; they are only ever declared with admiral_df().

Usage

infer_dataset_class(dataset)

Arguments

dataset

A data frame

Default value

none

Value

A character scalar: one of "ADSL", "BDS", "OCCDS", "TTE", "ADDL", "MDBDS", "MDTTE", "MDOCCDS", or "other"; or NA if the dataset has no records and its variables do not decide the class.

Details

A dataset is first classed as device data or subject data:

  • Device data contains SPDEVID, the device identifier, populated (neither NA nor "") for every record. Its class is one of the medical device classes "ADDL", "MDBDS", "MDTTE", and "MDOCCDS".

  • Subject data is otherwise data which contains all the subject keys (get_admiral_option("subject_keys"), by default STUDYID and USUBJID). Its class is one of "ADSL", "BDS", "OCCDS", and "TTE".

A dataset which is neither is "other". This keeps a data frame which merely shares variable names with an ADaM dataset – a coding dictionary with AETERM/AEDECOD columns, a summary table with PARAMCD and AVAL – from being taken for one.

The subject keys do not decide the class: in the ADaMIG-MD STUDYID is required in a device dataset and USUBJID is conditional, so a device dataset may identify the subject of every record. Nor does the presence of SPDEVID, as subject datasets record it too, e.g. the device involved in an adverse event; but there it is populated only for the records which involve a device. A subject dataset in which every record involves a device (e.g. an ADAE restricted to device-related events) is therefore inferred as device data, so declare its class with admiral_df() instead.

Within each class the following precedence is used. The order matters, because the classes are not mutually exclusive by variable content – a TTE dataset contains PARAMCD just as a BDS one does, and an occurrence dataset which has had a parameter added is structurally both.

  1. "TTE"/"MDTTE" – contains PARAMCD, CNSR, and STARTDT. Tested first because a time-to-event dataset is a BDS dataset by variable content; only the censoring and origin-date variables distinguish it.

  2. "BDS"/"MDBDS" – contains PARAMCD and AVAL or AVALC.

  3. "OCCDS"/"MDOCCDS" – does not contain PARAMCD, and contains a --DECOD/--TERM variable with a two-letter SDTM domain prefix (AEDECOD, DETERM, ...; a variable merely ending in TERM does not count), an AOCCxxFL occurrence flag, or TRTEMFL.

  4. "ADSL"/"ADDL" – does not contain PARAMCD and has one record per subject (per combination of the subject keys) or per device (per combination of STUDYID and SPDEVID). This is decided by the records: treatment variables are no evidence of ADSL, as BDS/OCCDS derivations merge them on from ADSL.

  5. "other" – none of the above, if there is at least one record.

  6. NA – none of the above.

See also

Other internal: admiral-package, extract_duplicate_records(), format.basket_select(), infer_class_by_structure(), new_admiral_df(), signal_duplicate_records()
